teams.heading: Vakatawa's early try in vain as Fiji lose Pacific Nations Cup final
teams.body: Fiji's bid for a third consecutive Pacific Nations Cup title ended in heartbreak after a late Samisoni Tua try condemned them to a 20-15 defeat against Japan in Tokyo on Saturday. Despite losing Mesake Doge to a first-half yellow card, the Flying Fijians led 12-10 at the interval through tries from Virimi Vakatawa and hooker Tevita Ikanivere. Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula locked the scores at 15-15 with a penalty midway through the second half, but the visitors could not hold out as the Brave Blossoms struck late to reclaim the trophy.

lead.why: The Flying Fijians suffered a narrow, hard-fought defeat to Japan in the Pacific Nations Cup final in Tokyo.

teams.heading: England Women held to draw as historic winning run reaches conclusion
teams.body: The Red Roses’ remarkable 39-match winning run came to an end on Friday after being held to a 26-26 draw by Canada at Sandy Park. Despite tries from Claudia Moloney-MacDonald, Hannah Botterman and Bryony Field, John Mitchell’s side could not overcome a relentless Canadian effort in the WXV Global Series fixture. Canada become the first team to avoid defeat against England since the 2022 World Cup final, though the team remains unbeaten in 40 Tests.

lead.why: The end of England's 39-match winning streak is a significant historical shift for the national programme.

teams.heading: France Women stun Australia with incredible second-half recovery in Aix-en-Provence
teams.body: The France Women's rugby team secured a dramatic 29-26 victory against Australia on Saturday, overcoming both a 19-point deficit and a bizarre mid-match delay caused by a burning bus outside the Stade Maurice David. Despite a period of severe disciplinary trouble that saw the hosts reduced to 11 players, France clawed back momentum after half-time. Captain Pauline Bourdon Sansus helped steer the team to 17 unanswered points in the final 25 minutes to snatch an unlikely win.

teams.heading: Ireland Women surrender 19-point lead in WXV defeat to United States
teams.body: The Ireland Women's rugby team suffered a disappointing 40-36 defeat against the United States in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium. Despite building a commanding 31-12 lead early in the second half, Scott Bemand’s side succumbed to a late USA comeback as disciplinary issues and a numerical disadvantage took their toll. Bemand noted that the loss was "a game we should have won," emphasising that his side must refine their technical process to maintain control for the full 80 minutes.

teams.heading: Italy women dominate Japan with emphatic 55-21 WXV Global Series win
teams.body: The Italy women's rugby team opened their WXV Global Series campaign with a comprehensive 55-21 victory over Japan at Stadio Omero Tognon. The Azzurre secured their largest-ever winning margin against the Sakura XV, highlighted by a prolific first-half burst that saw the hosts score three tries in seven minutes. Captain Vittoria Ostuni Minuzzi marked her 50th cap with a try, as Italy proved clinical in a match where they outplayed their opponents in all facets of the game.

lead.why: This is the most significant recent international result for Italian rugby, despite the focus on the men's team.

teams.heading: Scotland Women suffer heavy defeat as New Zealand run in ten tries
teams.body: Scotland Women struggled to contain a clinical New Zealand side, falling to a 66-14 defeat at Hive Stadium on Friday. Despite two first-half tries from Evie Gallagher, the visitors’ pace proved too much for the Scottish defence. New Zealand dominated the encounter with 10 tries, effectively ending the match as a contest before half-time. Scotland now turn their attention to a meeting with Australia at the same venue this Saturday, looking to bounce back from successive tournament losses.

lead.why: Scotland Women suffered a heavy defeat to New Zealand in their most recent WXV Global Series outing.

teams.heading: Wales Women deliver statement eight-try victory against South Africa in Cardiff
teams.body: Wales Women set a new standard on Friday, producing an expansive display to dismantle South Africa 50-19 in their WXV Global Series opener. Coach Sean Lynn’s side, who had endured a nine-match winless streak, ran in eight tries as Sisilia Tuipulotu and player of the match Alex Callender starred. Lynn described the performance as the start of a “new DNA” for the team, built on improved skill development and a refreshed attacking intent ahead of their next test.

teams.heading: Jordan Petaia returns to Wallabies squad after brief NFL football stint
teams.body: Jordan Petaia has rejoined the Wallabies squad for this week's one-off Test against South Africa. The utility back, who recently joined the Urayasu D-Rocks, previously left Australian rugby to pursue an NFL career with the Los Angeles Chargers. Petaia revealed his American football tenure was cut short due to a misdiagnosed hamstring injury that required a period of rehabilitation. Head coach Les Kiss has included the 26-year-old in a 34-man group as Australia look to continue their current momentum.

teams.heading: Japan defeat Fiji in Tokyo to secure Pacific Nations Cup title
teams.body: Japan claimed their first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 after a 20-15 victory over Fiji at Prince Chichibu Memorial Stadium. Mamoru Harada and Ben Gunter scored early tries, before Samisoni Tua crossed for the winner with 10 minutes remaining. It was the Brave Blossoms' 5th win over Fiji in 22 encounters. Captain Naoto Saito described the breakthrough as a vital step, stating, "I'm glad we won today, and it's a great breakthrough to create history for Japan."

lead.why: Japan's first Pacific Nations Cup title since 2019 is a major milestone for the national team's development.

teams.heading: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea faces lengthy sideline spell after surgery
teams.body: New Zealand Rugby has confirmed that All Blacks skipper Ardie Savea will undergo surgery on a dislocated shoulder, with no definitive return date yet established. Savea sustained the injury during the third Test against the Springboks earlier this month. While his absence from next month's Bledisloe Cup fixtures was already known, his availability for the November Nations Championship is now in serious doubt. Rehabilitation for such procedures typically requires around six months, complicating the side's planning for the remainder of the year.

lead.why: The captain's confirmed long-term injury following the tour is the most significant news for the team.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus releases Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende home
teams.body: Coach Rassie Erasmus has confirmed that Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende will return to South Africa, missing the upcoming test against the Wallabies in Perth. Erasmus explained that the decision follows a heavy workload for the pair during the recent Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series against the All Blacks. The coach remains confident in the depth of his travelling squad, insisting there is sufficient cover to manage the absence of both first-choice players for the fixture.

lead.why: The squad rotation of two high-profile starters ahead of the upcoming test is the most significant news for the team's immediate selection.
